reason: REQUEST CHANGES. Verified 14 existing-source claims with direct evidence at commit 20aefa1 (matches stated baseline exactly); all proposed scanner/inventory/policy capabilities are correctly absent (NET_NEW) and the spec labels them as proposed, not existing. However 3 blocking issues survive: (1) docs/SCOPED-VERIFIER.md already exists (committed a867fdd) documenting an unrelated Codex-subprocess re-entry guard for issue #8/#15 — the spec's Files-to-Change row 'Document audit boundaries, outputs and exclusions' does not acknowledge this collision, risking conflation of two unrelated authorization docs under one filename. Rename the target doc or add explicit reconciliation language before implementation. (2) The 'Exact mapping families from the current installer' table's 'scripts/nightshift-*.py -> Nightshift target' row is incomplete: install.sh:475 additionally installs nightshift-project-context.py to the Claude target as a second, explicitly-named destination not covered by any generic loop. Since the spec asserts the inventory module becomes 'the single owner of the file/tree mappings currently implemented by install.sh loops' and forbids a second independent destination list, make_inventory() must special-case this file or it will silently omit a real installed copy from scanning/ownership. (3) 'Early no-write --check' omits that the CURRENT install.sh already performs a filesystem write (mkdir -p CMD_DST/SCRIPT_DST/AGENT_DST at install.sh:293) inside the unconditional 'Existing conflicts' section that runs before today's ACTION=check exit (install.sh:345-348) — the Files-to-Change row for install.sh ('Consume shared mapping; early read-only check') does not call out removing/reordering this existing mkdir, so acceptance criterion 6 ('no filesystem writes... on fresh and existing targets') is not achievable by simply inserting an earlier scanner call; the pre-existing conflict-check mkdir must be explicitly relocated after the check exit or the criterion will fail on first test run. All three are blocking design/documentation gaps, not implementation bugs (none exist yet) — request changes to the spec before implementation begins.

claims.claim: Implementation baseline commit 20aefa116003134f6464b2673ab11f8a06e9e353 matches current checkout HEAD exactly.

install-links.json direction: keys are DESTINATION paths, values are SOURCE paths (dict(zip(dst_list, src_list))), matching 'Reuse install-links.json as ownership evidence... source equality against the current shared inventory'.

install_tree records tree installs into the same INSTALL_PAIRS (dst,src) structure as install_one, so 'symlink installation still uses the tree operation' and tree records exist in install-links.json at the tree root, not per-descendant.

Exact mapping families table entry 'scripts/nightshift-*.py | Nightshift target: scripts/<basename>' is incomplete: nightshift-project-context.py is additionally installed to the Claude target via an explicit named call, a second destination not produced by any generic loop and not represented in the table.

Files-to-Change entry 'docs/SCOPED-VERIFIER.md | Document audit boundaries, outputs and exclusions' does not acknowledge that this exact file already exists (committed a867fdd) with unrelated content: Codex-subprocess re-entry guard for factory orchestration resolving issue #8/#15, not branding/inventory scan boundaries.

'ACTION=check ... exits with its result before dependencies, mkdir, conflicts, hook checks... or writes' omits that the CURRENT install.sh unconditionally executes mkdir -p on CMD_DST/SCRIPT_DST/AGENT_DST inside the 'Existing conflicts' block, which runs before today's ACTION=check exit — a preexisting write in the exact path acceptance criterion 6 requires be write-free.

Retired-name patterns are currently assembled from string fragments in the test fixture itself ('cx'+'eng', 'con'+'nexure', 'drew'+'-pipeline', 'drew'+'-') so the fixture doesn't self-trip the audit, matching 'Assemble banned fixture literals from fragments so scanner fixtures do not themselves fail the maintained-source audit.'

Existing alias-preservation fixture in tests/test-branding.sh symlinks retired command/skill/bin aliases plus one unrelated symlink and asserts the retired ones are archived while the unrelated one is preserved — matches 'preserve existing alias-preservation fixtures' and 'Extra unrelated sibling plugins... remain unread and unchanged.'
want_codex() includes RUNTIME=local, and the post-install help text prints Codex-flavored guidance for local, matching 'Preserve order and runtime selection, including local using the Codex skill.'

Real YAML frontmatter in agent role files has no model: key; the substring 'model:' appears only inside an explanatory HTML comment below the frontmatter block, confirming the necessity of 'Frontmatter checks distinguish actual keys from explanatory comments.'

routing.json defines a 'cross_provider' policy under the adversarial route requiring actual --author-provider provenance and a different-provider fallback, corroborating the Sources claim of 'architect routing and independent cross-provider review policy.'

docs/PROJECT-CONTEXT.md documents NIGHTSHIFT_PROJECT_DIR as the neutral runtime variable with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR as a legacy ingress fallback, and an 'Optional document capability' section pushing provider-specific names into adapter-supplied mappings, matching 'finalized neutral project identity, convention reconciliation and optional document capability boundaries' and 'no provider MCP identifier in core.'

scripts/nightshift-project-context.py resolve_project() reads NIGHTSHIFT_PROJECT_DIR as neutral input and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR only as legacy fallback (raising PROJECT_CONFLICT if both set and differ), matching 'Issue 18 permits legacy inputs only through scripts/nightshift-project-context.py and documented compatibility readers.'

agents/nightshift-run-all-tests.md requires reading every path in a discovered conventions array including both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md when present, matching 'Its legitimate role prose mentions both applicable convention files.'

commands/nightshift-product.md resolves an optional 'document-read' capability through the runtime adapter, matching 'Its document capability asks adapters for actual tool mappings, with no provider MCP identifier in core.'

.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml already loops over tests/test-*.sh (which matches tests/test-branding.sh) plus runs evals/run-tests.sh, matching 'Existing CI discovery in .github/workflows/shellcheck.yml already executes this test; no second workflow is needed' and acceptance criterion 8's 'existing offline regression harness.'

install.sh already uses exit code 64 for invalid-argument failures ('Unknown flag'), corroborating the proposed convention 'exit 64 means invalid arguments/policy' as consistent with existing precedent.
scripts/nightshift-install-inventory.py exists as a shared pure inventory module with make_inventory(project, runtime, targets).
scripts/nightshift-branding.py exists as the scanner CLI with --project/--inventory source|installed|all.
scripts/nightshift-branding-policy.json exists as reviewed rule definitions and exceptions.

make_inventory() function, its version/entries schema (category/kind/source/destination/source_relative/logical_path) and category labels claude_commands/shared/shared_roles/claude_adapters/codex_skill/launcher exist anywhere in the codebase.
A retired slash-command detection family 'identified by issue 19' and a 'targeted stale ADR form' pattern exist in the current retired-pattern set.
